ga-nau-dong-bac-bo.name: Northern Vietnamese Chicken Aspic
ga-nau-dong-bac-bo.serving_basis: One medium bowl for four people, served with rice and pickled vegetables.
ga-nau-dong-bac-bo.description: Chicken is gently braised with pork rind and chicken feet to set the broth naturally, then combined with wood ear mushrooms, shiitake and black pepper. Once chilled, the clear aspic holds its shape. This is a familiar cold-weather and Tết dish in Northern Vietnam. Bếp Việt has scaled the home-style method to four servings.
ga-nau-dong-bac-bo.finished_dish: Tender chicken and lightly crisp wood ear mushrooms sit in a clear, softly set aspic with a gentle shiitake aroma.
ga-nau-dong-bac-bo.serving: Chill until fully set, then turn out onto a plate or spoon into portions. Serve cold with hot rice, pickled mustard greens or pickled scallions.
tips: Blanch and rinse the bones, chicken feet and pork rind before simmering for a clearer broth.
Keep the simmer gentle and skim regularly; season lightly because cold food tastes more strongly seasoned.
Cool promptly in a shallow covered container, refrigerate, and do not leave at room temperature for an extended period.
ga-nau-dong-bac-bo.image_alt: A clear glass bowl of Northern Vietnamese chicken aspic with chicken, wood ear mushrooms, shiitake and carrot flowers.
ga-nau-dong-bac-bo.time_note: About 5 hours 55 minutes, including 80 minutes of cooking and 4 hours of chilling; it can be made a day ahead.

ingredients.name: Boneless chicken
ingredients.notes: Cut into bite-size pieces; keep chilled until preparation.

ingredients.name: Chicken bones
ingredients.notes: Rinse, blanch briefly and rinse again.

ingredients.name: Chicken feet
ingredients.notes: Clean and blanch with the bones to help the broth set naturally.

ingredients.name: Pork rind
ingredients.notes: Scrape clean, blanch and cut into short strips; it contributes natural gelatin.

ingredients.name: Dried wood ear mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Rehydrate, rinse and slice thinly.

ingredients.name: Dried shiitake mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Soak until tender, remove tough stems and slice.

ingredients.name: Carrot
ingredients.notes: Cut into thin flowers for the base of the mould; optional.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For simmering the bones, chicken feet and pork rind; top up with hot water if needed.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Begin with a light amount and adjust to taste.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Starting amount; adjust after tasting the broth.

ingredients.name: Seasoning powder
ingredients.notes: Optional; use sparingly.

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.notes: Crush lightly; reserve some to finish the mould.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For sautéing the shallots.

preparation_steps: Blanch the chicken bones, feet and pork rind in boiling water for about 3 minutes, discard the water and rinse well. Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces; rehydrate the mushrooms and prepare the optional carrot.
Mince the shallots and slice the mushrooms. Set out a heavy pot and a clean, dry bowl or mould.
cooking_steps: Put the bones, chicken feet, pork rind and 1.6 litres of water in a pot. Bring to a boil, skim, then simmer partially covered over low heat for 50–55 minutes. Strain the clear stock; discard the bones and slice the softened rind.

Sauté the shallots in oil until fragrant. Add the chicken and stir until its surface changes colour. Season with fish sauce, salt, optional seasoning powder and some of the pepper, then add both mushrooms.
Pour in the strained stock and add the sliced rind. Cover and gently simmer for 20–25 minutes, until the chicken is just tender and the liquid is slightly reduced. Skim as needed and taste.
Arrange the optional carrot in the mould, then ladle in the chicken, mushrooms and broth. Let it cool briefly, cover and refrigerate for 3–4 hours until set. Finish with the remaining pepper.

ga-hap-la-sen.name: Chicken Steamed in Lotus Leaves
ga-hap-la-sen.serving_basis: One platter of steamed chicken for four, served with rice and vegetables.
ga-hap-la-sen.description: Chicken is seasoned with shallot, garlic, fish sauce and pepper, wrapped in lotus leaves and steamed until cooked through. The leaves gently perfume the chicken while the steam keeps it moist. Bếp Việt includes lotus seeds and shiitake as optional additions for a family-style platter.
ga-hap-la-sen.finished_dish: Juicy, tender chicken with a light lotus-leaf fragrance, complemented by soft lotus seeds and aromatic shiitake.
ga-hap-la-sen.serving: Open the lotus leaves while hot and spoon the steaming juices over the chicken. Serve at once with steamed rice and, if desired, lime-pepper salt.
tips: Wipe the leaves clean and briefly blanch them so they soften and are less likely to tear when wrapped.
Cut the chicken through the joints and avoid splintering the bones; steam until the thickest pieces are fully cooked.
If the lotus leaves are small, overlap two leaves and place the folded seam underneath.
search_terms: Vietnamese chicken steamed in lotus leaves
ga-hap-la-sen.image_alt: Vietnamese chicken steamed in opened lotus leaves, with lotus seeds and shiitake mushrooms on a platter.
ga-hap-la-sen.time_note: About 75 minutes, including a 15-minute marinade and 35 minutes of steaming; actual steaming time depends on piece size.

ingredients.name: Free-range chicken
ingredients.notes: A small chicken, jointed into serving pieces; thighs and wings help keep the meat moist.

ingredients.name: Fresh lotus leaves
ingredients.notes: Rinse, wipe dry and briefly blanch to soften.

ingredients.name: Fresh lotus seeds
ingredients.notes: Remove the bitter green germ; soak dried seeds first if substituting.

ingredients.name: Dried shiitake mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Soak until tender, rinse and halve.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Adjust to the saltiness of the brand.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Starting amount; adjust to taste.

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.notes: Use moderately so it does not mask the lotus fragrance.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Mix with the seasonings to coat the chicken evenly.

preparation_steps: Clean and joint the chicken into pieces of similar size. Pat dry. Clean the lotus leaves, soften briefly in hot water and pat dry.
Mix the shallot, garlic, fish sauce, salt, pepper and oil. Coat the chicken and leave for 15 minutes. Soak the shiitake and prepare the lotus seeds if using.
cooking_steps: Lay the lotus leaves in a steamer-safe dish, overlapping them to form a cradle. Arrange the chicken, lotus seeds and mushrooms inside, then fold the leaves over the top.
Bring the steamer water to a steady boil. Steam covered for about 30–35 minutes, turning the larger pieces once if needed, until the thickest part is thoroughly cooked and the juices run clear.
Rest for 5 minutes, open the leaves carefully to release steam, then transfer the chicken to a platter. Spoon over the cooking juices and garnish with scallion if desired.

mien-ngan-mang-kho-ha-noi.name: Hanoi Glass Noodles with Duck and Dried Bamboo Shoots
aliases: Hanoi duck and bamboo shoot vermicelli
mien-ngan-mang-kho-ha-noi.serving_basis: Four bowls of glass noodle soup with duck and dried bamboo shoots.
mien-ngan-mang-kho-ha-noi.description: A Hanoi-style bowl combines tender ngan duck, chewy glass noodles and softened dried bamboo shoots in a clear duck broth. Bếp Việt follows the published home-cooking method and scales it to four portions; the dried shoots require an overnight soak and repeated boiling before cooking.
mien-ngan-mang-kho-ha-noi.finished_dish: A clear, savoury broth with tender duck, fragrant bamboo shoots and springy glass noodles, finished with scallions and herbs.
mien-ngan-mang-kho-ha-noi.serving: Place blanched glass noodles in warm bowls, add sliced duck and bamboo shoots, then ladle over the boiling broth. Finish with scallions, coriander and a squeeze of lime; serve chili on the side.
tips: Soak dried bamboo shoots overnight, then boil and rinse them more than once until tender and mild-smelling.
Simmer the duck gently and skim the broth; a rolling boil can make the stock cloudy.
Blanch the glass noodles separately just before serving so they do not become waterlogged in the stock.
search_terms: Vietnamese glass noodle soup with duck
mien-ngan-mang-kho-ha-noi.image_alt: A blue-and-white bowl of Hanoi glass noodle soup with sliced ngan duck, dried bamboo shoots, scallions and herbs.
mien-ngan-mang-kho-ha-noi.time_note: About 10 hours 10 minutes total, including an 8-hour soak for the dried bamboo shoots; active preparation and cooking take about 2 hours 10 minutes.

ingredients.name: Ngan duck
ingredients.notes: Choose a medium bird, clean it and remove the oil gland; retain the bones for stock.

ingredients.name: Dried bamboo shoots
ingredients.notes: Soak for 6?8 hours or overnight; boil in fresh water until tender and the water is clear.

ingredients.name: Dried glass noodles
ingredients.notes: Soak until just pliable, rinse and cut shorter if needed.

ingredients.name: Dried shiitake mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Soak until soft and rinse; slice if using in the soup.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.notes: Roast or dry-toast whole until fragrant, then remove any charred skin.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.notes: Rinse and crush; use some to clean the duck.

ingredients.name: Pork fat or cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For saut?ing the bamboo shoots; use a moderate amount.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Rinse and chop; the white ends may be blanched separately.

ingredients.name: Culantro (saw-leaf herb)
ingredients.notes: Rinse and slice thinly.

ingredients.name: Coriander
ingredients.notes: Rinse and chop for serving.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For poaching the duck and making the soup stock; adjust for evaporation.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Divide between cleaning the duck and seasoning the stock.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Add near the end to retain its aroma.

ingredients.name: Seasoning powder
ingredients.notes: Optional; it may be replaced with salt and fish sauce.

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.notes: Sprinkle over the bowls just before serving.

ingredients.name: Fresh chili
ingredients.notes: Use to taste, or serve with chili vinegar.

preparation_steps: Soak the dried bamboo shoots in plenty of water overnight. Drain, boil for 20–30 minutes, rinse and repeat with fresh water until softened and free of a strong raw smell; drain and shred.
Clean the duck, rub with salt and crushed ginger, rinse and drain. Soak the glass noodles as directed, then cut into manageable lengths. Rinse and prepare the herbs.
cooking_steps: Put the duck in a pot with enough water to cover, a little ginger and shallot. Bring to a gentle boil, skim, then simmer until tender, about 45–60 minutes depending on the bird. Lift out the duck and strain the broth.

When cool enough to handle, remove the duck meat from the bones and slice. Sauté the bamboo shoots with a little oil, shallot and fish sauce until fragrant; add a ladle of broth and simmer for 10 minutes.
Return the bamboo shoots to the stock and simmer gently for another 10–15 minutes. Taste and adjust with fish sauce, salt and pepper; keep hot.

Blanch the glass noodles briefly in boiling water and divide among four bowls. Top with duck and bamboo shoots, ladle over the hot broth and finish with scallion and coriander. Serve with lime and chili.

vit-rang-rieng.name: Duck Stir-Fried with Galangal
vit-rang-rieng.serving_basis: One platter of duck for four, served with rice and vegetables.
vit-rang-rieng.description: Bone-in duck is marinated with fresh galangal, lemongrass and familiar Vietnamese seasonings, then browned and cooked until tender. The galangal-forward preparation appears on Hanoi duck menus; Bếp Việt adapts a published recipe for a four-person home meal and does not claim it is unique to the region.
vit-rang-rieng.finished_dish: Golden-brown duck pieces with lightly crisped skin, tender meat and an aromatic galangal-lemongrass coating.
vit-rang-rieng.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice and a lightly dressed cucumber or blanched greens. Offer lime-pepper salt on the side if desired.
tips: Use a heavy pan and brown the duck in batches so it sears instead of steaming.
Slice the galangal thinly or pound it coarsely so its aroma infuses the duck without overwhelming the meat.
Cook bone-in duck fully until tender; add small splashes of hot water if the pan dries before the pieces soften.
vit-rang-rieng.image_alt: Golden-brown Vietnamese duck pieces cooked with sliced galangal and lemongrass in a ceramic bowl.
vit-rang-rieng.time_note: About 90 minutes total, including a 25-minute marinade and about 40 minutes of cooking; timing varies with the size of the pieces.

ingredients.name: Duck
ingredients.notes: Clean, remove the oil gland and cut through the joints into serving pieces.

ingredients.name: Fresh galangal
ingredients.notes: Peel, rinse and pound; divide between the marinade and final stir-fry.

ingredients.name: Lemongrass
ingredients.notes: Remove tough outer layers, rinse and mince.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince.

ingredients.name: White rice wine
ingredients.notes: Rub over the duck with salt to help clean it; rinse thoroughly afterward.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Use in the marinade and adjust at the end.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Divide between cleaning and seasoning.

ingredients.name: Seasoning powder
ingredients.notes: Optional; can be replaced with salt.

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.notes: Use freshly ground if available.

ingredients.name: Fresh chili
ingredients.notes: Slice and add to taste; optional.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For pan-frying the duck and frying the aromatics.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Cut into short lengths and add at the end.

preparation_steps: Rub the duck with salt and a little crushed ginger if available, then rinse and pat very dry. Cut into similar-sized serving pieces.
Slice the galangal and lemongrass; mince the shallot and garlic. Mix fish sauce, sugar, pepper and optional fermented rice paste to make the marinade.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil in a wide, heavy pan. Add the duck in batches over medium to medium-low heat; turn regularly until browned and thoroughly cooked, about 25?30 minutes. Cover briefly if needed so the bone-in pieces cook through.
Transfer the duck to a plate and drain excess fat, leaving a thin film in the pan. Add the lemongrass, shallot, garlic and half the galangal; stir-fry over low heat until fragrant.

Return the duck with the remaining galangal and optional chili. Toss for 3?4 minutes until the aromatics coat the pieces and the pan is nearly dry. Adjust the fish sauce, finish with scallions and serve hot.

ngong-gia-cay-ha-noi.name: Hanoi-Style Goose Braised Giả Cầy
aliases: Goose braised with galangal and fermented rice
ngong-gia-cay-ha-noi.serving_basis: One pot of braised goose for four, served with rice or rice noodles.
ngong-gia-cay-ha-noi.description: Goose is briefly charred, then marinated with galangal, lemongrass, fermented rice and shrimp paste before being braised until tender. Hanoi catering and restaurant menus document goose prepared giả cầy; the listing is evidence that the dish is served locally, not proof that it is exclusive to Hanoi. Bếp Việt has adapted the method to a four-person household pot.
ngong-gia-cay-ha-noi.finished_dish: Tender goose with lightly charred skin in a thick, fragrant sauce of galangal, lemongrass, fermented rice and shrimp paste.
ngong-gia-cay-ha-noi.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice or fresh rice noodles. Add herbs and sliced chili at the table; adjust the shrimp-paste aroma with lime if desired.
tips: Char the skin lightly rather than burning it; wipe away soot before cutting the goose into pieces.
Use fermented rice and shrimp paste sparingly at first, then adjust after the sauce has simmered.
Keep the braise at a gentle simmer and add hot water in small amounts if the pot reduces before the goose is tender.
ngong-gia-cay-ha-noi.image_alt: A ceramic bowl of Hanoi-style goose braised giả cầy with golden-brown goose, galangal and lemongrass.
ngong-gia-cay-ha-noi.time_note: About 1 hour 55 minutes total, including 20 minutes of marinating and about 65 minutes of cooking; larger pieces may need longer.

ingredients.name: Goose
ingredients.notes: Cut into serving pieces; skin-on pieces add aroma and richness.

ingredients.name: Fresh galangal
ingredients.notes: Peel, pound or coarsely blend; divide between the marinade and braise.

ingredients.name: Fermented rice (m?)
ingredients.notes: Strain to remove coarse solids.

ingredients.name: Shrimp paste
ingredients.notes: Dissolve in a little warm water and add gradually; saltiness varies by brand.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Add lightly after tasting the shrimp paste.

ingredients.name: Lemongrass
ingredients.notes: Mince or slice thinly; B?p Vi?t adds a little to soften the poultry aroma.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Starting amount; it may be unnecessary if the shrimp paste is salty.

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.notes: Grind moderately and add near the end.

ingredients.name: Hot water
ingredients.notes: Add gradually during braising to keep the sauce thick.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Use to sear the goose only if the skin is lean.

preparation_steps: Clean the goose and pat dry. Char the skin lightly over a flame or hot pan, turning all sides; wipe away any soot, then cut the goose into serving pieces.
Pound or slice the galangal, bruise and slice the lemongrass, and mince shallot and garlic. Dissolve the shrimp paste in a little water if needed; mash the fermented rice until smooth.
cooking_steps: Mix the goose with galangal, lemongrass, fermented rice, shrimp paste, fish sauce, salt and pepper. Leave to marinate for 20 minutes.

Heat a heavy pot. Add a little oil only if the goose is lean, then add the goose and marinade. Stir over medium heat until the pieces tighten and the galangal becomes fragrant. Add the remaining galangal and lemongrass.

Add hot water to about halfway up the meat, cover slightly ajar and braise gently for 45?55 minutes, turning occasionally, until tender. Uncover and reduce until the sauce is glossy; taste and adjust acidity and salt, then serve hot.
